title: Unexpected region cycling triggered a fallback wave leading to high-latency and model variant overload — postmortem
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket documents the incident that occurred on 2026-03-03 where our routing subsystem began rapidly cycling regional weights for a subset of customer clusters, which triggered a chained fallback to cheaper model variants. The immediate effect was a region flapping pattern that increased cross-region tail latency and overloaded variant-serving pools, causing elevated 5xxs and timeouts for multiple tenants. This postmortem covers detection, impact, root cause, mitigations, permanent fixes, and action items.
incident_summary: At ~2026-03-03T06:17:00Z, routing weight adjustments for eu-west-1 started oscillating for traffic from the EU control plane. The control-plane signal interpreted temporary telemetry gaps as sustained capacity loss, aggressively draining region weight. Traffic was re-routed to fallback tiers and model variants; fallback pools (variant-v2-quant) reached saturation. Overloaded fallback pools experienced increased inference latency and queueing, causing a cascade where other regions also drained to pick up load, amplifying the problem into a routing wave. Total customer requests impacted: ~7% of active calls globally for ~23 minutes.
impact_metrics: Error rate spike: baseline 0.3% -> 6.9% at peak
P95 latency increased from 210ms -> 1.9s across affected routes
Fallback pool CPU/GPU queue depth: 7x normal
timeline: 2026-03-03T06:17:00Z - First anomalous regional weight delta observed by routing telemetry (eu-west-1).
2026-03-03T06:18:20Z - Automated drain policy started applying escalating weights; regional controller created drain tombstones for several nodes.
2026-03-03T06:19:05Z - Smart routing moved 18% of eu-west-1 traffic to fallback tier; fallback variant pools started to queue.
2026-03-03T06:21:10Z - On-call alerted via PagerDuty after error-rate alert fired for 'inference.5xx_rate' and 'routing.fallback_surge'.
2026-03-03T06:22:30Z - Manual hold placed on drain propagation (control-plane override), rollback of decay constant to previous safe value initiated.
2026-03-03T06:28:45Z - Drain dampening and hysteresis patches applied to control plane via emergency config; fallback throttles engaged to shed non-critical work.
2026-03-03T06:40:40Z - System stabilized; regional weights neutralized and fallback queues drained. Post-incident monitoring continued for 48 hours.
root_cause: A bug was introduced in the regional capacity aggregator (PR merged 2026-02-25) that incorrectly treated tombstoned node capacity as expired but still counted it towards 'available_capacity' for a short window. This produced noisy telemetry: short gaps were amplified as sustained capacity loss due to a regression in the moving-average windowing logic (the window size was accidentally reduced from 90s to 9s in one path). The routing decision engine reacted to the noisy signal using the recent 'aggressive decay' weight-update configuration, which has a large step size for faster failover. The combination of compressed smoothing window + aggressive decay allowed small transient telemetry glitches to drive full-region drains. When traffic was redirected, fallback variant pools were not protected by a strong circuit breaker: they accepted traffic until queue saturation, which increased latency and error rate, feeding back into routing decisions and causing other regions to take similar actions (cascading amplification).
immediate_mitigation: 1) Control-plane override to freeze all drain changes for eu-west-1 and related locality buckets. 2) Rollback of the moving-average window change to the previous 90s value. 3) Applied temporary damping multiplier to 'decay_step' for routing updates. 4) Engaged variant-pool throttles to reject or delay non-critical batched requests. 5) Directed customer-support to open high-touch communications for impacted customers.
long_term_fix: 1) Revert and harden the capacity aggregator; add unit and integration tests that simulate tombstone lifecycles and ensure no double-counting or short-window artifacts. 2) Add a conservative lower-bound on moving-average window sizes enforced at config-load time. 3) Implement a per-variant circuit breaker that limits ramp-up rate and enforces queue-length backpressure before accepting extra traffic. 4) Add hysteresis and a per-minute bounded reweighting cap to the smart routing policy to prevent >10% weight changes per minute for any region. 5) Create a staging chaos test that injects short telemetry gaps and validates routing stability.
action_items: ENG-185010: Add integration tests for tombstone lifecycle and moving-average windowing (owner: Rohan Patel) - due 2026-03-17
ENG-185011: Implement per-variant circuit breaker with queue-length metrics exported (owner: Mei Chen) - due 2026-03-24
ENG-185012: Limit max per-minute regional reweighting in routing service (owner: Daniel Kim) - due 2026-03-20
ENG-185013: Build staging chaos harness for telemetry gaps (owner: Saira Ahmed) - due 2026-03-31
ENG-185014: Create alert for 'fallback_surge' that includes variant-pool saturation and per-region reweight delta (owner: Reliability Team) - due 2026-03-14
postmortem_notes: Corrective config was kept for 48 hours and rolled into routing-2.4.0 after tests passed.

We found two near-misses in the prior month where reduced smoothing caused micro-flaps but were suppressed by conservative decay; those incidents were not escalated. We will surface similar near-misses in the future via a weekly signal-stability dashboard.
Design decision: keep aggressive decay config behind an opt-in flag for specific customers that require fast failover; default remains conservative.
